study: Worth/Sizmur/Walker/Bradshaw/Styles 2017 (NFER eval), Teacher Observation (CMPO/RANDA TOWER), EEF
eval_evidence: EEF efficacy trial independently evaluated by NFER; the intervention was delivered by a separate provider, the Centre for Market and Public Organisation (CMPO), University of Bristol.
developer_evidence: CMPO (the delivery org) trained lead teachers, who then ran the peer-observation programme in their departments; the trial team did not deliver the observations to classroom teachers (p.9).
cascade_evidence: CMPO researchers trained lead teachers from maths and English departments, and lead teachers cascaded/organised the RANDA TOWER peer observations among department teachers (train-the-lead-teacher, ≥1 extra hop).
counterfactual_evidence: 'Almost three-quarters of the control group schools were already doing some peer observation' — controls used a similar existing practice, so the contrast is against an active/contaminated counterfactual (p.6).
coaching_evidence: Intervention was structured peer observation among teachers plus software training; no ongoing in-class coaching of teachers by the developer/provider.
student_dose_evidence: Intervention changes only teacher practice (peer observation of teaching); no tutoring, pull-out, extra minutes, or student-facing software dose.
maturity_evidence: Intervention designed as a defined two-year block of peer observation; primary GCSE outcome measured at its end for the two-year-exposure cohort, with no separate prior-rollout maturity wave.
